title: Beatrice d'Aragona to Eleonora d'Aragona, Buda, 8 March 1486 (DECODE R1142)

steps.what: Extracted five exact dates, recipients and shelfmarks from cached DECODE metadata; web reader could not open live DECODE page.
Retrieved Cryptiana index and Berzeviczy 1914 OCR. Located 8 March 1486 letter in no. LVI, not yet compared to cipher.
Used existing user-authorized DECODE cookie to acquire all 18 images. R1143 has repeated photographs with decipherment slips moved.
Located MDE III nos. 10 and 12 for both 1482 letters, III no. 75 for May 1486, IV supplement no. 45 for March cipher and III no. 54 for its closing.

Matched dates, clear wording, cipher boundaries and R1143 manuscript slips to older readings. Rendered print confirms italics and March Virtus/Fortis/M. markers. No exhaustive key verification claimed.

Entry split from beatrice1482 under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R1142 announces a change of cipher, and its alphabet looks different from the 1482 one; not grouped with R1143 either, whose key is not shown to be the same.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): the OCR extracts of the printed decipherment (MDE IV 1878, MDE III 1877) and of the plain body (Berzeviczy 1914) as decryptions; no glyph transcription of the cipher exists (project work).

Vestigia's cipher original (1967) and period clear copy (1998) compared. The Virtus/Fortis/M./decus markers of the 1878 print are Latin-letter decoy words inside the cipher runs (wrnſ, forts…, M), underlined by the period decipherer: nulls. Pre-registered identity test: the 1482 key (beatrice1482) on these runs gives characters 0.135 against best 0.253 of 200 shuffled keys, so the old cipher is not the 1482 alphabet (211 signs; identity test only).

Integration check of PR #620. Identity test re-run with beatrice1482/vestigia/measure.py: 0.135 against best 0.253 of 200 shuffled keys on 211 signs; weak by construction (105 of the 211 signs have no value in the 1482 key, 86 of them labelled as Latin letters or words). Vestigia image of the clear copy 1998 opened: Virtus, fortis, M. and decus are there and underlined, a word struck before 'preposta'. That they are nulls is the contributor's reading of the underlining; a code word is not excluded. Cipher image 1967 not sampled; Cremonini 2015/2018 and Berzeviczy 1908 (listed by Vestigia) not opened. The key of the old cipher is not rebuilt.

outcome.method_basis: The cipher passages were already deciphered in print in MDE IV (1878), supplement no. 45, the closing in MDE III no. 54 and the plain body in Berzeviczy (1914) no. LVI; the prints were matched to the DECODE images and no key was applied.
outcome.notes: Andriolo to be brought to Hungary (the editor links the negotiation to the Djem affair). The printed reading keeps unexplained Virtus/Fortis/M. markers. Split on 14 Oct 2026 from beatrice1482. 14 Nov 2026: Virtus/Fortis/M. explained as decoy words (nulls) flagged in the period copy; the old cipher is not the 1482 alphabet.

texts.label: Buda, 8 March 1486
texts.summary: Beatrice of Aragon to her sister Eleonora of Ferrara: the cipher passages concern bringing Andriolo to Hungary, paying his travel and honouring the king's promises (the 1878 editor ties the negotiation to the Djem affair); the plain body is on Ippolito d'Este's appointment to Esztergom and Cardinal Ascanio's opposition, and the closing says the letter uses the old cipher and encloses a new one. Decryptions: uncorrected OCR of MDE IV (1878) suppl. no. 45 (cipher passages), MDE III (1877) no. 54 (closing) and Berzeviczy (1914) no. LVI (plain body).

prior.where: MDE IV (1878), supplement no. 45, pp. 367-368 (the cipher passages); MDE III (1877) no. 54, p. 67 (the closing); Berzeviczy (1914) no. LVI (the plain body)
